summary: RE-VERIFICATION of the 4 security fixes from iteration_28 plus a full regression re-run of the RBAC/JWT-forgery/IDOR/injection matrix. 387 pytest security cases executed against the public URL: 387 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. All 3 previously EXPECTED-FAILING tests now PASS. All 4 reported fixes are CONFIRMED effective and no regression was introduced. Zero new HTTP 500s in the backend log during the run (the 4 UnknownHashError/500 traces in backend.err.log are stale, emitted at log lines 2415-3612 during the iteration_28 audit, before the fix). No application code was modified.

minor.issue: LOW (carried over from iteration_28, still not fixed): 7 endpoints still declare untyped `data: dict` bodies (admin.py:276/297/330, applications.py:236/284/348/918) and therefore bypass Pydantic validation. I actively fuzzed all of them with Mongo operators, wrong scalar types and empty bodies (13 cases) - none returned 500 and none bypassed authz, so this is NOT currently exploitable. It remains a defence-in-depth / maintainability gap: replace with explicit Pydantic models.

LOW (carried over): lockout is keyed on ip:email, so a distributed attacker rotating source IPs is not throttled per account. Verified working as designed (5 x 401 then 429, lock persists). Consider an additional per-account counter.

action_items: No blocking action required - all 4 reported vulnerabilities are verified closed.

OPTIONAL/LOW: convert the 7 remaining `data: dict` request bodies (admin.py:276/297/330, applications.py:236/284/348/918) to Pydantic models. Fuzzing showed no 500s and no authz bypass today, so this is hardening only.
OPTIONAL/LOW: add a per-account (IP-independent) brute-force counter on /api/admin/login.

DEPLOYMENT REMINDER: TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET must also be set on the VPS AND passed to Telegram setWebhook (secret_token param), otherwise real Telegram callbacks will be rejected with 403 in production.
critical_code_review_comments: FIX #1 verified in employee.py download_document: the `contract-` branch now checks `payload.role != 'admin' and contract.employee_email != payload.sub -> 403`. Owner and admin still get 200 with content-type application/pdf. Note the check uses employee_email vs JWT `sub` while get_documents still matches contracts via the brittle employee_id.replace('emp-','EMP').upper() mangling - the two paths use different matching rules; consider unifying to avoid a future divergence like the one that caused this IDOR.

FIX #2 verified in applications.py: `ApplicantLogin(BaseModel)` with EmailStr/str replaces the untyped dict. Operator payloads now short-circuit at FastAPI validation (422) and never reach find_one, so passlib can no longer be handed a dict (no more UnknownHashError 500).
FIX #3 verified in test_sessions.py:48 `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` -> 43-char tokens, unique across creations, full public lifecycle intact.

FIX #4 verified in chat.py telegram_webhook: guard is env-conditional (`if expected_secret:`). It is now active because the env var is set, but the endpoint still fails OPEN if TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is ever missing/empty. Recommend failing closed (reject with 503/403 when the secret is unset) so a misconfigured deploy cannot silently re-open the webhook.

rca_of_the_issue: All four iteration_28 findings are resolved at the code level and confirmed behaviourally. Root causes and their fixes: (1) the IDOR existed because ownership checks were added in contracts.py but the parallel contract-serving path in employee.py was missed - now it compares contract.employee_email to the JWT sub with an admin bypass; (2) applications/login had never been migrated to a typed body like admin/employee login, so Mongo operators flowed into find_one and passlib raised UnknownHashError (500) - a Pydantic EmailStr model now rejects them at validation time with 422; (3) the public session token was uuid4().hex[:12] (48 bits) and is now secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (~256 bits); (4) the Telegram webhook guard was inert because TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET was absent from backend/.env - the value is now set, activating the check. Residual risk is limited to the env-conditional (fail-open) design of the Telegram guard and the remaining untyped dict bodies, neither of which is exploitable in the current configuration.
